lines.trans: You should just go back to work and earn some money!
That was the money to feed Toru rice!
In the end, without money, you can't even be free.

meanings.note: Points to something visible farther away from both speaker and listener.

examples.trans: That over there is a school.

meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
i-adjective; used alone as 'Shut up!'.

examples.text: うるさいな、静かにしろ。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Polite/standard form of 金 (かね) with honorific prefix お.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Casual/intimate apology, often softened with な or ね.
Standard heartfelt apology.

examples.text: ごめんなさい、もうしません。
examples.trans: I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses frustration, regret, or surprise that reality contradicts what was expected; often trails off at the end of a spoken complaint.

examples.text: 約束したのに来なかった。
examples.trans: Even though they promised, they did not come.

examples.text: せっかくの休みなのに。
examples.trans: Even though it is a hard-earned day off.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Introduces a stunned guess ('don't tell me... / surely you aren't...').

examples.text: まさか来ないとは思いませんでした。
examples.trans: I never thought they wouldn't come.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb.

examples.text: 仕事に戻って稼いでくれ。
examples.trans: Go back to work and earn money.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Rustic, affectionate term for father.

examples.text: 父ちゃんが帰ってきた。

meanings.note: Potential stem + そう (稼げそう) means 'looks like one can earn well'.

examples.text: しっかりお金を稼ぎます。
今月はよく稼げました。
examples.trans: I was able to earn well this month.

meanings.note: Refers to rice as a staple food or grain.

meanings.en: in the end; after all; ultimately
meanings.note: Used when summing up what a situation comes down to.

examples.text: 結局、金がないと自由にもなれないんだな。
examples.trans: In the end, without money, you can't even be free.

examples.text: 結局、彼には会えませんでした。
examples.trans: In the end, I couldn't meet him.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; causative 食べさせる can mean 'to feed/support'.

examples.text: 朝ごはんを食べましたか。
家族を食べさせるために働く。
examples.trans: I work to support my family.

meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb; 黙ってろ! is a rough 'Shut up!'.
